headline: Andrew Wielandt holds L1 Long Short Fund (LSF) in his SMSF, citing strong long-term returns and Australian-focused long/short strategy
reasoning: Wielandt recommends LSF as a way to access the alternatives/hedge fund exposure that the Future Fund (at 12-15% of its portfolio) uses. LSF is managed by L1 Capital in Melbourne, has approximately $2.8 billion FUM, and runs an absolute return strategy with around 70% Australian exposure and 30% offshore, holding 50-100 positions. The fund has returned over 50% in the last 12 months and approximately 17% per annum over five years. headline: Andrew Wielandt holds L1 Long Short Fund (LSF) in his SMSF, noting the discount to NAV has narrowed but returns have been approximately 17% per annum.
reasoning: Wielandt references LSF as one of three LITs held in his SMSF under a Future Fund-style methodology. He notes that while LSF was previously trading at a discount to asset backing, that discount has narrowed significantly so investors now pay close to a dollar for a dollar of assets. The fund is analyst-focused rather than systematic, meaning manager stock-picking skill is a key risk factor. It is part of a 12-15% alternatives sleeve designed to smooth portfolio returns and provide downside cover.
